e-5673.knowledge_point: Calculating the Number of Permutations of Objects Chosen From a Group Fewer Than Ten
e-5673.problem: In a horse race with $8$ horses, how many different ways can the gold, silver, and bronze medals be awarded?
e-5673.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
_{n}P_r = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $8$ horses, so $n=8.$ We want to select $3$ of those horses for gold, silver, and bronze, so we have $r=3.$ 

Therefore, the number of different ways to award the medals is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{8}{P}_{3} & =\frac{8!}{(8-3)!} \\  & =\frac{8!}{5!} \\  & =\frac{8\cdot 7\cdot 6\cdot \cancel{5!}}{\cancel{5!}} \\  & =8\cdot 7\cdot 6 \\  & =336.\end{aligned}
$$

e-5674.problem: A company has $20$ employees. A total of $4$ employees are needed to fill the roles of president, vice president, treasurer, and secretary. How many different ways can this be achieved?
e-5674.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
_{n}P_r = \frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $20$ employees, so $n=20.$ We want to select $4$ of those employees to fill the roles of president, vice president, treasurer, and secretary, so we have $r=4.$

Therefore, the number of different ways to fill the roles is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{20}{P}_{4} & =\frac{20!}{(20-4)!} \\  & =\frac{20!}{16!} \\  & =\frac{20\cdot 19\cdot 18\cdot 17\cdot \cancel{16!}}{\cancel{16!}} \\  & =20\cdot 19\cdot 18\cdot 17 \\  & =116\,280.\end{aligned}
$$

The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $6$ digits, so $n=6.$ We want to select $4$ of those digits for the passcode, so we have $r=4.$

$$

$$

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: Ashley has $5$ tasks. She decides to do one on Thursday and another on Friday. How many different choices of the two tasks does Ashley have?
after.worked_solution:
The number of permutations of $n$ objects taken $r$ at a time is given by the formula

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.
$$

There are $5$ tasks to choose from, so $n=5.$ We want to select $2$ of those for Ashley to do, so we have $r=2.$ 

Therefore, the number of different choices is

$$
\begin{aligned}{}_{5}{P}_{2} & =\frac{5!}{(5-2)!} \\  & =\frac{5!}{3!} \\  & =\frac{5\cdot 4\cdot \cancel{3!}}{\cancel{3!}} \\  & =5\cdot 4 \\  & =20.\end{aligned}
$$

There are 11 people taking an online quiz at the same time. How many ways can people finish in first, second, and third place, assuming there are no ties?

a
990
b
450
c
1880
d
900
e
720
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The number of permutations of n objects taken r at a time is given by the formula nPr=n!(n−r)!.

There are 11 people, so n=11. We want to select 3 of those people to come first, second, or third, so we have r=3.

Therefore, the number of different ways to place the people is

11P3=11!(11−3)!=11!8!=11⋅10⋅9⋅8!8!=11⋅10⋅9=990.

$$
{}_{n}{P}_{r}=\frac{n!}{(n-r)!}.

$$

$$
